name: Point To Visual
what_you_see: Creator on screen in frame 1 immediately points (finger or both hands) up/sideways at a product, graphic or text block that sits beside/above them.
why_it_works: Gaze-and-gesture cueing: viewers reflexively follow a pointing finger to the target.
how_to_shoot: Green-screen or split the frame: creator bottom half points up at a product shot or claim text top half.
detection_cues: 0s creator visible with arm rising; 0.5s index finger extended toward an off-body object/graphic; 1s target element fully shown; 1.5s creator still pointing or talking.

name: Move In Frame
what_you_see: Frame starts empty or on a background; the creator walks/leans/steps into shot from an edge within the first second, often ending close to lens.
why_it_works: Motion onset is the strongest pre-attentive attention trigger; an empty frame filling creates mini-anticipation.
how_to_shoot: Lock phone on tripod, start recording on empty kitchen/bathroom, walk in holding the product and stop at mid-shot.
detection_cues: 0s empty/near-empty background; 0.5s body part entering from edge; 1s subject centered; 1.5s subject static and talking/holding product.

name: Camera Whip
what_you_see: Frame 1 is a fast horizontal/vertical camera swing with heavy motion blur that snaps to the subject or product.
why_it_works: Blur-to-sharp resolution creates a mini 'arrival' moment; motion blur reads as energy.
how_to_shoot: Handheld: start pointed at wall, whip fast to product on counter and stop hard; add whoosh SFX.
detection_cues: 0s heavy directional blur; 0.5s blur resolving; 1s sharp subject/product; 1.5s stable framing.

name: Jump In
what_you_see: Creator physically jumps/leaps into the frame from the side or from below, landing in position to talk.
why_it_works: Sudden large-body movement + surprise entry = startle response.
how_to_shoot: Tripod shot at counter height; creator crouches below frame and springs up holding the product.
detection_cues: 0s empty or partial frame; 0.5s body mid-air/entering fast from edge; 1s landed, facing camera; 1.5s talking/holding product.

name: Snap/Pop Reveal
what_you_see: A snap, clap or gesture instantly makes the creator or product appear (jump cut on the action).
why_it_works: Impossible instant change breaks expectations; the gesture signals 'magic' and payoff.
how_to_shoot: Film hand snap on empty table, cut on the snap, second clip same framing with product sitting there.
detection_cues: 0s hand gesture/empty scene; 0.5s snap/clap frame; 1s product/person suddenly present in identical framing; 1.5s hold on product.

name: Clone Body Double
what_you_see: Two (or more) copies of the same person in one frame at once, often interacting (one asks, one answers).
why_it_works: Impossible image forces a double-take; implies dialogue/argument structure.
how_to_shoot: Tripod locked, film creator on left then right, mask together in CapCut; one plays skeptic, one holds product.
detection_cues: 0s two identical people visible; 0.5s both moving independently; 1s dialogue gesture between them; 1.5s one holds product.

name: Fly on Wall
what_you_see: Subject is looking off screen (not at lens) mid-conversation, like an interview or podcast clip, framed from a side angle.
why_it_works: Voyeur effect: feels like overhearing something real rather than being sold to.
how_to_shoot: Seat founder/customer at 45 degrees, interviewer off camera; open on a mid-answer punchy line about the product.
detection_cues: 0s subject eyeline off-lens; 0.5s mouth moving mid-sentence; 1s mic or second person implied; 1.5s no direct address.

name: Anticipated Disaster
what_you_see: Opening clip shows something dangerous/bad about to happen to someone (spill, fall, crash) and cuts/stitches away right before or at impact.
why_it_works: Threat detection + need for closure: brain must see the outcome.
how_to_shoot: Film a full glass teetering at table edge or phone about to drop, cut to creator with the protective product.
detection_cues: 0s precarious object/person; 0.5s motion toward danger; 1s hard cut before/at impact; 1.5s new scene/creator.
source: Kallaway collection (Short-Form Lego Bricks DB, https://www.scribd.com/document/1064813825); 'Impending Disaster' name per brief

name: Object Catch
what_you_see: An object flies into frame from off-screen and the creator catches it, usually the product.
why_it_works: Unpredicted incoming motion triggers reflexive tracking.
how_to_shoot: Off-camera helper tosses product; creator catches at chest height and starts talking.
detection_cues: 0s creator idle; 0.5s blurred object entering frame; 1s hands closing on object; 1.5s product held up to lens.

name: Using Random Product (Pope In The Pool)
what_you_see: Creator talks while doing an unrelated, visually odd task (e.g., in a pool, juggling, peeling fruit) that is not the topic.
why_it_works: Subconscious incongruity keeps eyes busy while the audio delivers the hook.
how_to_shoot: Founder delivers the pitch while ironing, feeding a goat, or floating in a pool - product appears later.
detection_cues: 0s person doing a physical task unrelated to caption; 0.5s continued task + talking; 1s no product yet; 1.5s task continues.
source: Kallaway collection (Short-Form Lego Bricks DB, https://www.scribd.com/document/1064813825); also https://thebrandaudit.ca/blogs/news/10-visual-hooks-to-stop-the-scroll

name: Setting Down Phone
what_you_see: First frames are shaky as the recording device is placed on a surface, then settle on the creator already talking.
why_it_works: Feels raw/unscripted (native, not an ad) and implies urgency.
how_to_shoot: Hold phone, record while placing it against the bathroom mirror/car dash, then start the pitch.
detection_cues: 0s tilted/shaky frame, maybe hand filling frame; 0.5s camera settling; 1s stable frame with creator; 1.5s talking.
search_keywords: so I have to tell you

name: Holding Prop
what_you_see: Creator starts holding or staring at an object close to camera; the object dominates the frame.
why_it_works: Object curiosity + gives the eye a concrete focus before words.
how_to_shoot: Open with the product held 20cm from the lens, creator glancing at it then camera.
detection_cues: 0s object in hand filling 1/3+ of frame; 0.5s creator eyes on object; 1s object rotated/shown; 1.5s talking.

name: Many of Same Prop
what_you_see: Frame filled with many units of the same (or similar) item - a pile, grid, or stack.
why_it_works: Abundance/scarcity signal and pattern density demand a second look.
how_to_shoot: Arrange 30 units of the product on bed or counter, creator sits behind them.
detection_cues: 0s repeated identical items fill frame; 0.5s creator or hand among them; 1s items still dominant; 1.5s one item picked up.

name: Framebreaker
what_you_see: Subject is cut out and layered so part of it (hand, product, head) breaks over the border of a framed photo/box, appearing 3D.
why_it_works: Depth illusion violates the flat-screen expectation.
how_to_shoot: Rotoscope the hand holding product so it pokes out of a white-bordered card over a blurred background.
detection_cues: 0s visible inner frame/border; 0.5s subject part crossing border edge; 1s layered depth clear; 1.5s motion continues outside frame.

name: Jump Switch
what_you_see: Creator jumps; on landing, the location/outfit/product has changed.
why_it_works: Action-matched change feels seamless and surprising.
how_to_shoot: Jump in old clothes, cut at apex, land wearing product/in new room.
detection_cues: 0s creator crouching/jumping; 0.5s mid-air; 1s landing in different setting/outfit; 1.5s pose.

name: 3P Crash Zoom
what_you_see: A shot of another person (third person) in the distance with a fast push/zoom in onto them.
why_it_works: Rapid scale change toward a target signals 'this person matters'.
how_to_shoot: Film customer across a room/street using the product, digitally crash-zoom to them.
detection_cues: 0s wide shot with a small distant person; 0.5s rapid zoom motion; 1s person fills frame; 1.5s action/reaction visible.

name: Fridge POV
what_you_see: Camera placed inside a fridge/cabinet/drawer/shelf; the door opens or item is removed to reveal the creator looking in.
why_it_works: Unusual vantage point + 'being seen by an object' novelty.
how_to_shoot: Put phone on fridge shelf behind the product; creator opens door and grabs product.
detection_cues: 0s dark or interior view of shelves; 0.5s door opening/light flood; 1s creator face looking in; 1.5s hand reaches for product.
source: Kallaway collection (Short-Form Lego Bricks DB, https://www.scribd.com/document/1064813825); also https://www.scribd.com/document/904349354/60-Visual-Hooks-1

name: Write on Screen
what_you_see: A marker writes text directly on the lens/glass between camera and subject, or text is animated as if handwritten.
why_it_works: Watching text form creates suspense until the word completes.
how_to_shoot: Shoot through a glass pane; creator writes the benefit claim with a dry-erase marker.
detection_cues: 0s marker tip near lens; 0.5s partial letters; 1s word forming; 1.5s full word readable over subject.
source: Kallaway collection (Short-Form Lego Bricks DB, https://www.scribd.com/document/1064813825); also https://www.scribd.com/document/904349354/60-Visual-Hooks-1

name: Mirror
what_you_see: Creator addresses the audience via a mirror reflection; the phone may be visible.
why_it_works: Familiar get-ready framing reads native; reflection composition is visually layered.
how_to_shoot: Film skincare/apparel pitch in bathroom mirror with product on sink.
detection_cues: 0s mirror edges/reflection; 0.5s phone visible in hand; 1s creator talking to reflection; 1.5s product near face.

name: Body Swaps
what_you_see: Mid-action, the person on screen is replaced by another person in identical pose/framing (hard cut on action).
why_it_works: Identity discontinuity creates instant confusion to resolve.
how_to_shoot: Two creators repeat same movement holding product; cut on the action beat.
detection_cues: 0s person A in pose; 0.5s action beat; 1s person B in same pose/framing; 1.5s continues.
source: Kallaway collection (name given in brief; not found in public Kallaway docs - unconfirmed)

name: Object Into Lens
what_you_see: Product (or hand) moves rapidly toward the lens until it fills/blacks out the frame.
why_it_works: Looming motion triggers a defensive startle reflex.
how_to_shoot: Creator thrusts the product at the phone until it blocks the lens, cut to next shot.
detection_cues: 0s product small in hand; 0.5s product growing rapidly; 1s product fills/blurs frame; 1.5s cut to new shot.

name: Crumple/Throw at Camera
what_you_see: Creator crumples paper or tosses an object straight at the camera.
why_it_works: Looming object + aggression reads as startling.
how_to_shoot: Crumple a competitor's receipt/ad printout and throw at lens.
detection_cues: 0s paper/object in hand; 0.5s throwing motion; 1s object hits/approaches lens; 1.5s creator talking.

name: Slam/Drop Start
what_you_see: First frame: a hand slams a product/book on a table or drops something noisily, then speaking begins.
why_it_works: Sound-synced impact is a zero-edit pattern interrupt.
how_to_shoot: Slam the product box onto a desk in close-up, then tilt to creator.
detection_cues: 0s hand high with object; 0.5s impact on surface (bounce/shake); 1s camera settles; 1.5s creator talking.

name: Sunglasses On
what_you_see: Creator puts on sunglasses (or takes them off) in the first second before speaking.
why_it_works: Confident gesture + motion onset; meme-familiar.
how_to_shoot: Creator slides on shades while holding product, 'deal-with-it' vibe.
detection_cues: 0s hands raising glasses; 0.5s glasses on face; 1s pose; 1.5s speaking.

name: Sit Down Into Frame
what_you_see: Creator sits down into the frame (chair/car seat/floor) as the video starts.
why_it_works: Subtle movement grabs attention and signals 'settle in, this is a story'.
how_to_shoot: Creator drops into car seat or couch, product in hand.
detection_cues: 0s standing torso or empty chair; 0.5s body lowering; 1s seated at eye level; 1.5s talking.

name: Walking Backward Talk
what_you_see: Handheld selfie while walking (often backward) through a busy space, background moving.
why_it_works: Constant background motion keeps eyes engaged; feels vlog-native.
how_to_shoot: Founder walks through warehouse or street holding phone at arm's length.
detection_cues: 0s selfie framing, background motion; 0.5s parallax; 1s ongoing walk; 1.5s talking.

name: Hand Grab From Off-Screen
what_you_see: A hand enters the frame and grabs the product off a surface (or out of someone's hand).
why_it_works: Implied desire/competition for the item.
how_to_shoot: Static product shot, hand swoops in and snatches it.
detection_cues: 0s product alone on surface; 0.5s hand entering; 1s product lifted; 1.5s product out of frame or at lens.

name: Pour / Splash
what_you_see: Liquid, powder or cream being poured/splashed in close-up, often onto the product or a surface.
why_it_works: Fluid motion is hypnotic and satisfying.
how_to_shoot: Pour coffee on a stain-proof shirt; splash water on waterproof gear.
detection_cues: 0s container tilting; 0.5s liquid stream; 1s impact/splash; 1.5s result visible.

name: Destruction / Stress Test
what_you_see: The product (or rival) is hit, dropped, crushed, cut, burned, or run over in the first frames.
why_it_works: Violence to objects + 'will it survive?' curiosity.
how_to_shoot: Drop phone case from head height onto concrete; stand on the bottle.
detection_cues: 0s product in hazardous setup; 0.5s impact/force applied; 1s product under stress; 1.5s outcome partly visible.

name: Squeeze / Squish
what_you_see: Close-up of fingers squeezing, pressing, peeling, or stretching a soft product.
why_it_works: Tactile ASMR mirror-neuron satisfaction.
how_to_shoot: Macro shot of thumb pressing into memory foam or peeling a pimple patch.
detection_cues: 0s fingers on product; 0.5s deformation begins; 1s max squish; 1.5s rebound.

name: Rip-Open Unboxing
what_you_see: Hands tearing tape/box/bag open with product about to emerge.
why_it_works: Anticipation of reveal; TikTok names unboxing a proven opener.
how_to_shoot: Top-down shot of hands slicing the mailer and pulling the product out.
detection_cues: 0s sealed package; 0.5s tearing/cutting; 1s product partially visible; 1.5s product lifted.

name: Mid-Action Demo Start
what_you_see: Video begins with the product already working mid-task (vacuum sucking, blade cutting, serum applied).
why_it_works: Immediate proof; TikTok recommends showing the product in action right away.
how_to_shoot: Cut the first 2s of the demo clip away so frame 1 is peak action.
detection_cues: 0s product actively operating; 0.5s visible effect; 1s result progressing; 1.5s continues/cut.

name: Chase Sequence
what_you_see: Creator literally runs after the product (on a string, rolling, carried by someone).
why_it_works: Absurd literalism captures attention and dramatizes desire.
how_to_shoot: Tie product to fishing line and pull it away as creator chases.
detection_cues: 0s product moving away; 0.5s creator running behind; 1s chase continues; 1.5s grab or cut.

name: Post-It / Cover Reveal
what_you_see: Product (or answer) is hidden under a post-it, cloth or cardboard that is peeled/pulled away.
why_it_works: Curiosity gap: hidden object demands the reveal.
how_to_shoot: Stick a question post-it on product front; peel it in first second.
detection_cues: 0s covered object with note/cloth; 0.5s hand pulling cover; 1s product exposed; 1.5s product hero.
search_keywords: what are you doing this summer

name: Rock-Paper-Scissors / Coin Flip
what_you_see: Two creators play RPS or flip a coin on camera with labels (save money vs buy product).
why_it_works: Game outcome suspense; viewers predict the winner.
how_to_shoot: Label each hand with text overlay; product always 'wins'.
detection_cues: 0s two hands/coin; 0.5s shake/flip motion; 1s result; 1.5s product appears.

name: Stop-Hand To Lens
what_you_see: Creator shoves an open palm or 'stop' sign to the lens in the first frame.
why_it_works: Literal command gesture + looming hand.
how_to_shoot: Palm at lens, pull back to reveal product in other hand.
detection_cues: 0s palm fills frame; 0.5s hand pulls back; 1s creator visible; 1.5s product shown.

name: Tear / Rip Paper
what_you_see: Creator tears a page, contract, or printed 'rules' in half on camera.
why_it_works: Destruction + symbolic rejection.
how_to_shoot: Tear a printed competitor price list.
detection_cues: 0s paper held; 0.5s tearing starts; 1s two halves; 1.5s pieces falling.

name: Money Throw
what_you_see: Bills thrown into the air around creator.
why_it_works: Money is a primal attention magnet; chaos motion.
how_to_shoot: Toss prop cash while announcing a sale.
detection_cues: 0s hands with cash; 0.5s bills airborne; 1s bills falling across frame; 1.5s creator speaking.

name: Face Lean-In to Lens
what_you_see: Creator's face lunges toward lens into extreme close-up, eyes filling frame.
why_it_works: Intimacy/looming face triggers social attention circuits.
how_to_shoot: Lean in to whisper the 'secret' benefit.
detection_cues: 0s normal framing; 0.5s face approaching; 1s eyes/nose fill frame; 1.5s pull back or talk.

name: Problem Reenactment
what_you_see: Exaggerated acting out of the problem (hair frizz, back pain, spilling) before the product appears.
why_it_works: Instant self-identification with the pain.
how_to_shoot: Creator dramatically fails at the task the product fixes.
detection_cues: 0s person struggling/frustrated; 0.5s failure moment; 1s exaggerated reaction; 1.5s product intro or continue.

name: Wake Up / Bed Start
what_you_see: Creator lying in bed/on floor, often shot from above, before sitting up.
why_it_works: Vulnerable, unusual horizontal framing.
how_to_shoot: Top-down bed shot, creator sits up and grabs product from nightstand.
detection_cues: 0s horizontal body/top-down; 0.5s sitting up; 1s product reached; 1.5s talking.

name: A vs B Comparison Graphics
what_you_see: Screen divided with labels (e.g., 'Theirs' vs 'Ours', 'Before' vs 'After') and graphics/checkmarks on each side.
why_it_works: Comparisons trigger instant judgement; brain wants to pick a winner.
how_to_shoot: Left: competitor product with red X; right: yours with green check; labels at top.
detection_cues: 0s two panels with labels; 0.5s icons/checks animating; 1s one side highlighted; 1.5s holds.
source: Kallaway collection (Short-Form Lego Bricks DB, https://www.scribd.com/document/1064813825) ('A vs B Graphics' per brief)

name: Text Slide In
what_you_see: Headline text slides in from an edge over the opening footage within the first second.
why_it_works: Motion on text draws eye to message before audio.
how_to_shoot: Keyframe the benefit headline sliding in from left over product B-roll.
detection_cues: 0s footage without text or partial text; 0.5s text mid-slide; 1s text locked; 1.5s text static.

name: Interactive Title
what_you_see: Title text appears in an interesting way - creator pushes, catches, or is revealed from behind it.
why_it_works: Text becomes a physical object in the scene, breaking the 2D plane.
how_to_shoot: Creator 'pulls down' the headline like a blind to reveal product.
detection_cues: 0s creator hand near text zone; 0.5s text moving with gesture; 1s text set; 1.5s creator talking.

name: Text/Arrow Pointer
what_you_see: Arrow(s) and short label point at a detail in the image (a feature, a flaw).
why_it_works: Directs gaze precisely; implies something noteworthy hidden in plain sight.
how_to_shoot: Freeze on product close-up, red arrow + 'this saved me $300'.
detection_cues: 0s image with arrow graphic; 0.5s arrow pulsing/drawing; 1s label; 1.5s zoom toward target.

name: Small Image Drop Overlay
what_you_see: A small image (logo, product, face) drops/bounces onto a larger background image and integrates into it.
why_it_works: Unexpected element entering composition; scale contrast.
how_to_shoot: Drop a PNG of the product onto a lifestyle photo with bounce animation.
detection_cues: 0s base image; 0.5s small element falling/scaling in; 1s element settled; 1.5s text or voice.

name: Screen Recording w/ Motion
what_you_see: Starts with a phone/desktop screen recording that zooms/pans to guide the eye to a specific element.
why_it_works: Familiar UI + motion guidance; implies proof or tutorial.
how_to_shoot: Screen-record the Shopify order notification or review page and zoom on the key number.
detection_cues: 0s UI screen; 0.5s zoom/pan motion; 1s highlighted UI element; 1.5s cursor/touch.

name: Image Overlay Motion
what_you_see: Begins on an image (with or without Ken Burns motion) plus text headline instead of live video.
why_it_works: Clean readable composition delivers the idea instantly.
how_to_shoot: Use a striking product photo with slow zoom and bold claim text.
detection_cues: 0s still image + text; 0.5s subtle zoom; 1s still image; 1.5s cut to video.

name: Countdown
what_you_see: On-screen numbers 3, 2, 1 before revealing something.
why_it_works: Countdowns create built-in anticipation and a promised payoff.
how_to_shoot: Big 3-2-1 over covered product, reveal on 'go'.
detection_cues: 0s large '3'; 0.5s '2'; 1s '1'; 1.5s reveal.

name: Bold Headline Text Box
what_you_see: Large high-contrast text block (white box/black text or outlined) dominating the top third from frame 1.
why_it_works: Readable in silent autoplay; frames the value instantly.
how_to_shoot: Overlay a 6-8 word claim in TikTok-native font over any UGC opener.
detection_cues: 0s big text present; 0.5s same; 1s same; 1.5s maybe swaps line.

name: Comment Reply Bubble
what_you_see: TikTok/IG comment bubble overlaid on frame (e.g., 'Those seem so extra') with creator reacting beside it.
why_it_works: Social conflict + native UI; viewers want to see the response.
how_to_shoot: Use TikTok 'reply with video' sticker to a real objection comment.
detection_cues: 0s comment bubble UI; 0.5s creator reacting; 1s bubble persists; 1.5s demo starts.

name: Fake Text / iMessage Thread
what_you_see: iMessage/WhatsApp/DM bubbles popping in over footage asking about the product.
why_it_works: Voyeurism into private conversation + social proof.
how_to_shoot: Animate a friend asking 'where did you get that??' bubble by bubble.
detection_cues: 0s chat UI; 0.5s bubble appears; 1s reply bubble; 1.5s cut to product.

name: Social Post Screenshot
what_you_see: A tweet/Reddit post/Amazon review card fills the screen or sits over the creator (green-screen style).
why_it_works: Borrowed credibility and relatable complaint.
how_to_shoot: Green-screen creator in front of a Reddit thread about the problem.
detection_cues: 0s post card with UI chrome; 0.5s highlight/zoom on text; 1s creator reaction; 1.5s talk.

name: Star Rating / Review Card
what_you_see: 5 gold stars and a quoted review line over product footage.
why_it_works: Instant social proof heuristic.
how_to_shoot: Stars animate in one by one over hero shot.
detection_cues: 0s stars graphic; 0.5s stars filling; 1s quote text; 1.5s product.

name: Price Slash / Sale Tag
what_you_see: Old price with animated strike-through and new price or '% OFF' badge.
why_it_works: Loss aversion and deal-seeking.
how_to_shoot: Animate red slash over $89, show $39.
detection_cues: 0s price text; 0.5s slash line drawing; 1s new price; 1.5s product.

name: Numbered Listicle Title
what_you_see: Big number + list headline ('3 reasons your skin...') with number '1' marker.
why_it_works: Promises finite, skimmable payoff.
how_to_shoot: Title '5 things I wish I knew before buying X', '#1' tag on first item.
detection_cues: 0s number headline; 0.5s item #1 label; 1s first visual; 1.5s continues.

name: Circle / Highlight Annotation
what_you_see: Hand-drawn red circle or highlight box around a detail, often with zoom.
why_it_works: Mimics YouTube thumbnail cues: 'something is here'.
how_to_shoot: Circle the stain before/after or the tiny label.
detection_cues: 0s image; 0.5s circle drawing; 1s zoom into circle; 1.5s hold.

name: Kinetic Typography
what_you_see: Words pop/scale in one at a time, synced to speech or beat, dominant on screen.
why_it_works: Rhythmic reading keeps eyes locked.
how_to_shoot: CapCut auto-captions with bounce animation and keyword color.
detection_cues: 0s single big word; 0.5s next word; 1s next word; 1.5s phrase complete.

name: Big Stat Callout
what_you_see: Giant number (e.g., '93%' or '$10,000') occupies the frame.
why_it_works: Specific numbers imply evidence and scale.
how_to_shoot: Show '2,000,000 sold' counter animating up.
detection_cues: 0s large number; 0.5s counter moving; 1s label; 1.5s cut.

name: Checklist Tick
what_you_see: List items with checkboxes being ticked in sequence.
why_it_works: Completion satisfaction and quick info hit.
how_to_shoot: Benefits checklist ticking next to product.
detection_cues: 0s list; 0.5s first check; 1s second; 1.5s third.

name: Redacted / Censored Bar
what_you_see: Key word/brand hidden behind a black bar, blur, or emoji.
why_it_works: Withheld info creates curiosity gap.
how_to_shoot: Blur product name in the headline until reveal.
detection_cues: 0s text with bar/blur; 0.5s same; 1s hint; 1.5s reveal or hold.

name: Phone Screen Magic
what_you_see: A phone lies among products and text appears 'magically' on its screen.
why_it_works: Device screens pull gaze; magical appearance is unexpected.
how_to_shoot: Composite claim text onto phone screen in flat lay.
detection_cues: 0s phone screen blank; 0.5s text appears; 1s text readable; 1.5s products around.

name: Handwritten Sign / Paper Note
what_you_see: Creator holds a handwritten sign/paper with a message, possibly flipping it.
why_it_works: Low-fi human authenticity; readable without sound.
how_to_shoot: Hold sign 'I tried every acne cream' then flip to product.
detection_cues: 0s paper with handwriting; 0.5s creator holding it; 1s flip; 1.5s next message.

name: Whiteboard Explainer
what_you_see: Hand drawing a diagram on a whiteboard/paper in real time.
why_it_works: Watching a drawing form = process curiosity.
how_to_shoot: Sketch 'problem -> product -> result' quickly.
detection_cues: 0s marker on board; 0.5s lines forming; 1s partial diagram; 1.5s creator.

name: Search Bar Typing
what_you_see: Search bar UI with a query being typed and autocompleted.
why_it_works: Familiar UI mirrors the viewer's own question.
how_to_shoot: Animate 'how to get rid of...' typing then show product.
detection_cues: 0s search bar; 0.5s letters typing; 1s full query; 1.5s results/cut.

name: Poll / Guess Sticker
what_you_see: Question with A/B options or a guess prompt overlaid on a mystery visual.
why_it_works: Invites participation; viewers commit to an answer.
how_to_shoot: Show extreme close-up of product texture with 'Guess what this is?'
detection_cues: 0s question overlay; 0.5s options; 1s mystery visual; 1.5s hint.

name: Breaking News Lower Third
what_you_see: TV-news style lower third/ticker ('BREAKING:') over footage.
why_it_works: Authority and urgency cues borrowed from news.
how_to_shoot: Creator as anchor with banner 'BREAKING: this sold out 3x'.
detection_cues: 0s red banner graphic; 0.5s ticker moving; 1s anchor framing; 1.5s continues.

name: Meme Caption Frame
what_you_see: Video letterboxed inside a white top bar with meme-style black caption.
why_it_works: Native meme grammar reads as entertainment, not ad.
how_to_shoot: Put funny relatable caption above product fail clip.
detection_cues: 0s white top bar text; 0.5s clip playing; 1s punchline motion; 1.5s continues.

name: Split Screen / Duet
what_you_see: Frame split into two (left/right or top/bottom) playing different clips simultaneously.
why_it_works: Two stimuli at once; comparison or reaction dynamic.
how_to_shoot: Top: problem footage; bottom: product fixing it.
detection_cues: 0s clear divider line; 0.5s both halves moving; 1s both active; 1.5s continues.

name: Spec Callout Lines
what_you_see: Product hero shot with thin lines/dots pointing to labeled features that draw in.
why_it_works: Premium tech-product aesthetic; organized information.
how_to_shoot: Rotate product and animate 3-4 feature callouts.
detection_cues: 0s product center; 0.5s lines drawing; 1s labels; 1.5s rotation.

name: Journal Story Highlight
what_you_see: Handwritten journal page with brand name highlighted by marker.
why_it_works: Intimate diary voyeurism + highlight draws eye.
how_to_shoot: Highlight product name in handwritten entry.
detection_cues: 0s journal page; 0.5s highlighter stroke; 1s brand highlighted; 1.5s page turn.

name: Motion-Tracked Text
what_you_see: Label/text pinned to a moving object/person via tracking.
why_it_works: Text feels part of the physical scene.
how_to_shoot: Track 'this is $12' to the bottle as creator waves it.
detection_cues: 0s text attached to object; 0.5s both moving together; 1s still attached; 1.5s continues.

name: Watch Till The End Text
what_you_see: Explicit 'wait for it' / 'watch till the end' overlay over teaser footage.
why_it_works: Explicit open loop commitment.
how_to_shoot: Overlay over satisfying build-up footage.
detection_cues: 0s overlay text; 0.5s footage building; 1s text persists; 1.5s continues.

name: Viral Stitch Linked Reaction
what_you_see: Opens on a recognizable viral clip, then cuts to creator reacting and linking it to the topic.
why_it_works: Borrowed attention from a proven clip + curiosity about the link.
how_to_shoot: Stitch a viral fail related to the problem, cut to founder: 'this is why we made X'.
detection_cues: 0s third-party viral footage (different quality/style); 0.5s peak moment; 1s cut to creator; 1.5s creator talking.

name: Match Cut
what_you_see: Rapid series of shots where shapes/positions/text line up across cuts.
why_it_works: Visual continuity with content change feels clever and hypnotic.
how_to_shoot: Product circle lid -> moon -> cup rim cuts aligned at center.
detection_cues: 0s shape centered; 0.5s cut, same shape/position new content; 1s another; 1.5s product.

name: Visual Switch
what_you_see: An action in shot 1 (cover lens, spin, clap) cleanly transitions into shot 2.
why_it_works: Continuity of motion masks the cut; payoff is the new scene.
how_to_shoot: Cover lens with product box, uncover in new setting.
detection_cues: 0s action beginning; 0.5s occlusion/motion peak; 1s new scene; 1.5s continue.

name: Beat Match Visual Switch
what_you_see: Clips switch exactly on music beats in the first seconds.
why_it_works: Audio-visual synchrony is pleasurable and propulsive.
how_to_shoot: Cut 4 product shots to a trending sound's beats.
detection_cues: 0s shot A; ~0.4s cut on beat; ~0.8s cut on beat; 1.2s cut on beat.
source: Kallaway collection (Short-Form Lego Bricks DB, https://www.scribd.com/document/1064813825) ('Beat Match Switch' per brief)

name: Viral Stitch Motion Match
what_you_see: Starts with a viral clip, then your footage matches its motion (e.g., same swing/throw).
why_it_works: Continuation illusion links borrowed attention to your brand.
how_to_shoot: Viral basketball throw clip -> your product caught in matching motion.
detection_cues: 0s viral clip motion; 0.5s motion peak; 1s your clip continues same direction; 1.5s product.

name: Viral Stitch Unlinked Switch
what_you_see: High-anticipation viral clip, then a cold hard cut to unrelated brand/business footage.
why_it_works: Anticipation from clip carries over; the jarring switch is itself the hook.
how_to_shoot: Open on a crazy stunt; cut before resolution to founder at desk.
detection_cues: 0s viral high-tension footage; 0.5s tension rising; 1s hard cut to unrelated brand scene; 1.5s creator talks.

name: Camera Wipe
what_you_see: Something (hand, object, person) passes across the lens, wiping the frame into a new scene.
why_it_works: Occlusion + reveal resets attention.
how_to_shoot: Swipe product across lens, reveal after-state.
detection_cues: 0s scene A; 0.5s object crossing frame; 1s scene B revealed behind wipe; 1.5s hold.
source: Kallaway collection (name given in brief; not found in public Kallaway docs - unconfirmed)

name: Rapid Flash Montage
what_you_see: 4-8 very short (0.1-0.3s) shots in the first 1.5 seconds.
why_it_works: Novelty density overwhelms scroll reflex.
how_to_shoot: Cut 6 product close-ups and reactions in 1.5s.
detection_cues: 0s shot A; 0.3s shot B; 0.6s shot C; 1s shot D; 1.5s shot E+.

name: Fake Ending / Cut to Black
what_you_see: Opens with or quickly hits a black screen/credits, then continues.
why_it_works: Violates expectation of a starting video.
how_to_shoot: Black frame with 'the end' then rewind to explain.
detection_cues: 0s black/end card; 0.5s black; 1s snap back to footage; 1.5s talk.

name: Fake Drop / Beat Drop Tease
what_you_see: Visual build-up then an abrupt freeze or hard cut when the beat should drop.
why_it_works: Violated anticipation and rhythm.
how_to_shoot: Slow product build-up, freeze at the drop, then reveal.
detection_cues: 0s rising motion/build; 0.5s intensifying; 1s abrupt freeze/cut; 1.5s reveal.

name: In Media Res Start
what_you_see: Video begins mid-sentence/mid-argument/mid-chaos with no setup.
why_it_works: Missing context forces viewer to catch up.
how_to_shoot: Start on creator mid-rant with product in hand.
detection_cues: 0s speaker mid-motion with no intro; 0.5s continued; 1s context ambiguous; 1.5s context building.

name: Fake Crash / Phone Drop
what_you_see: The camera appears to fall/crash; frame tumbles, cracks, or goes black.
why_it_works: Simulated accident = startle and concern.
how_to_shoot: Film phone dropping onto a bed, add crack overlay, cut to case ad.
detection_cues: 0s normal shot; 0.5s violent tilt/spin; 1s impact/crack/black; 1.5s recovery.

name: Freeze Frame Record Scratch
what_you_see: Action freezes suddenly (often with record-scratch), with a label or narration intro.
why_it_works: Classic sitcom trope; motion stop is jarring.
how_to_shoot: Freeze on creator mid-spill: 'yep that's me. you're probably wondering...'
detection_cues: 0s action in progress; 0.5s freeze; 1s freeze holds + text; 1.5s rewind or narrate.

name: Unexpected Interruption
what_you_see: A second person barges into frame/scene mid-speech.
why_it_works: Social disruption hooks curiosity about who and why.
how_to_shoot: Partner walks in: 'that tip you gave me worked'.
detection_cues: 0s creator talking; 0.5s door/second person entering; 1s interaction; 1.5s product.

name: Photo Collage to Video
what_you_see: Starts as a static collage of photos that snaps into live video.
why_it_works: Format switch resets attention.
how_to_shoot: Collage of customer photos animating into UGC clip.
detection_cues: 0s grid of photos; 0.5s still; 1s transition; 1.5s live video.

name: Multi-Creator Mashup
what_you_see: Rapid succession of different people each showing the product.
why_it_works: Social proof + face variety.
how_to_shoot: Cut 5 UGC creators saying one word each.
detection_cues: 0s person A with product; 0.4s person B; 0.8s person C; 1.2s person D.

name: Remote Control Channel Switch
what_you_see: A remote clicks and the scene/product variant changes stop-motion style.
why_it_works: Interactive feel; each click is a mini-reveal.
how_to_shoot: Click through each colorway of the product.
detection_cues: 0s remote pointed; 0.5s click; 1s new variant; 1.5s another click.

name: Genre Bait-and-Switch
what_you_see: Opens like a different genre (horror, nature doc, cooking show) then reveals it's a product ad.
why_it_works: Prediction error when genre breaks.
how_to_shoot: Nature-documentary style shot of 'wild' product, then cut to UGC.
detection_cues: 0s cinematic/genre styling; 0.5s genre cue; 1s tone break; 1.5s product.

name: Audio-Visual Mismatch
what_you_see: Visual contradicts sound or caption (calm scene + panic text, luxury look + 'cheap').
why_it_works: Cognitive dissonance forces resolution.
how_to_shoot: Show fancy spa scene while caption says '$9 from Amazon'.
detection_cues: 0s visual vs text/sound conflict; 0.5s same; 1s conflict emphasized; 1.5s explanation.

name: Transformation Cover Cut
what_you_see: Hand/cloth covers the lens then reveals a transformed look (hair, skin, room).
why_it_works: Instant before/after payoff.
how_to_shoot: Cover lens with palm, reveal after using product.
detection_cues: 0s before state; 0.5s cover; 1s after state; 1.5s pose.

name: Stitch Interview Mic-In-Face
what_you_see: Handheld mic thrust toward a stranger on the street, question asked.
why_it_works: Spontaneity and real-person reactions.
how_to_shoot: Ask shoppers 'what are you looking for?' and hand product.
detection_cues: 0s mic in foreground with stranger; 0.5s stranger reacts; 1s answer; 1.5s product.

name: Speed Ramp Effect
what_you_see: Footage speeds up then slows (or vice versa) across the transition from shot 1 to shot 2.
why_it_works: Time distortion is dynamic and cinematic.
how_to_shoot: Ramp a pour to slow-mo at splash.
detection_cues: 0s normal speed; 0.5s accelerated blur; 1s slow motion; 1.5s normal.

name: The Zoom In
what_you_see: Slow continuous zoom toward creator's face/product from frame 1.
why_it_works: Subtle intensification signals importance; cinematic tension.
how_to_shoot: Digital slow zoom 100->115% on founder saying the claim.
detection_cues: 0s medium shot; 0.5s slightly tighter; 1s tighter; 1.5s close.

name: Look Up At Camera // Top Down
what_you_see: Camera placed high in a room corner or overhead; subject looks up at it.
why_it_works: Unusual angle reads like security cam/surveillance.
how_to_shoot: Stick phone high on the kitchen wall, creator looks up.
detection_cues: 0s steep high angle; 0.5s subject tilting head up; 1s eye contact upward; 1.5s talk.

name: Sudden Danger 1P POV
what_you_see: First-person view of something dangerous heading toward the viewer (ball, car, dog), cut at the moment.
why_it_works: Self-threat triggers visceral startle.
how_to_shoot: POV of product flying at face, cut to creator.
detection_cues: 0s POV scene; 0.5s object approaching lens; 1s near impact/cut; 1.5s new scene.

name: Fish Eye
what_you_see: Barrel-distorted ultra-wide image, faces/products bulge at center.
why_it_works: Distortion is novel and playful.
how_to_shoot: Clip-on fisheye lens, product pushed to the camera.
detection_cues: 0s curved lines/bulged center; 0.5s movement exaggerated; 1s same; 1.5s same.

name: Frame Collapse
what_you_see: Black bars slide in top & bottom, collapsing frame into cinematic ratio, timed to a beat.
why_it_works: Framing change feels like a 'moment' begins.
how_to_shoot: Keyframe black bars closing on the beat before hero shot.
detection_cues: 0s full frame; 0.5s bars entering; 1s letterboxed; 1.5s hero shot.

name: Crazy Transitions
what_you_see: High-motion editing transitions: spins, zoom blurs, glitch, shake, from templates.
why_it_works: Visual energy + novelty.
how_to_shoot: Apply a CapCut trending template to product shots.
detection_cues: 0s shot with motion blur; 0.5s spin/zoom transition; 1s new shot; 1.5s another transition.

name: Experimental (Interactive)
what_you_see: On-screen motion graphics that suggest the viewer's thumb (swipe/tap), then the edit responds.
why_it_works: Hijacks the scrolling gesture itself; feels interactive.
how_to_shoot: Animate a fake 'tap here' hand icon; video 'responds' by zooming to product.
detection_cues: 0s hand/finger icon or fake UI; 0.5s simulated tap/swipe; 1s screen reacts; 1.5s content.

name: Color Switch
what_you_see: Opens in grayscale (0 saturation) and snaps to full color on a tap/beat.
why_it_works: Color onset is a strong pre-attentive trigger.
how_to_shoot: Grey 'before' scene turns vivid when product used.
detection_cues: 0s B&W frame; 0.5s B&W; 1s sudden full color; 1.5s color.

name: Snap Zoom / Zoom Punch
what_you_see: Instant zoom (jump or 2-4 frame ramp) into face/product on a key word.
why_it_works: Sudden scale jump = emphasis and jolt.
how_to_shoot: Punch in 130% on 'ONE product'.
detection_cues: 0s normal frame; 0.3s sudden tighter frame; 1s held; 1.5s back out.

name: Dolly Zoom
what_you_see: Subject stays same size while background stretches/compresses.
why_it_works: Uncanny spatial warping signals realization.
how_to_shoot: Walk phone backward while zooming in on product.
detection_cues: 0s subject centered; 0.5s background scale shifting; 1s strong warp; 1.5s done.

name: Reverse Footage
what_you_see: Motion plays backward - product flies up into hand, liquid returns to glass.
why_it_works: Physics violation.
how_to_shoot: Drop product, reverse clip so it jumps back into hand.
detection_cues: 0s object on ground/splash; 0.5s moving upward unnaturally; 1s lands in hand; 1.5s normal.

name: Freeze Frame
what_you_see: Motion stops dead on a frame with a highlight or text.
why_it_works: Motion-to-stillness contrast.
how_to_shoot: Freeze mid-splash with label.
detection_cues: 0s motion; 0.5s freeze; 1s freeze; 1.5s resume.

name: Stop Motion
what_you_see: Product moves in choppy frame-by-frame steps, assembling or walking itself.
why_it_works: Handcrafted novelty; objects 'alive'.
how_to_shoot: Shoot 20 photos moving product box, play at 12fps.
detection_cues: 0s product; 0.5s jumped position; 1s another; 1.5s another (no motion blur).

name: Slow Motion Hero
what_you_see: Ultra slow-motion of action (hair flip, splash, crumble).
why_it_works: Reveals invisible detail; luxurious feel.
how_to_shoot: 240fps shot of serum drop hitting skin.
detection_cues: 0s action starting slowly; 0.5s droplet/motion visible in detail; 1s still slow; 1.5s slow.

name: Time-lapse / Hyperlapse
what_you_see: Hours compressed into seconds (plant growth, cleaning, melting).
why_it_works: Visible change at unnatural speed.
how_to_shoot: Time-lapse of the stain vanishing over 30 minutes.
detection_cues: 0s scene; 0.5s rapid change; 1s more change; 1.5s near end.

name: Blur-to-Focus
what_you_see: Opens blurred (text or subject) and slowly/sharply comes into focus.
why_it_works: Brain needs to resolve unclear information.
how_to_shoot: Blurred claim on paper racks into focus; or foreground product racks to face.
detection_cues: 0s blurred frame; 0.5s partial focus; 1s sharp; 1.5s sharp.

name: Camera Shake Impact
what_you_see: Frame shakes violently on an impact or word.
why_it_works: Simulated physical force.
how_to_shoot: Add shake on product slam.
detection_cues: 0s stable; 0.5s violent jitter; 1s settle; 1.5s stable.

name: Glitch / VHS / Datamosh
what_you_see: Pixel smearing, RGB split, scan lines or datamosh artifacts.
why_it_works: Looks like a malfunction; brain checks.
how_to_shoot: Glitch transition into the product reveal.
detection_cues: 0s RGB split/scan lines; 0.5s pixel smear; 1s clean image; 1.5s clean.

name: Green Screen Composite
what_you_see: Creator cut out over an image/article/website/product page background.
why_it_works: Credibility of source + native TikTok look.
how_to_shoot: Creator over the product page or an article about the problem.
detection_cues: 0s creator edges over still background; 0.5s creator talking; 1s background shows headline; 1.5s pointing.

name: Jump Out of Phone
what_you_see: Creator appears to exit a phone/TV screen into the real world.
why_it_works: Impossible 2D-to-3D crossing.
how_to_shoot: Composite creator stepping out of phone with product.
detection_cues: 0s phone screen showing creator; 0.5s creator breaching screen; 1s in real room; 1.5s talking.

name: Multi-Screen Self Conversation
what_you_see: The same person on multiple screens (laptop, phone, monitor) talking to each other.
why_it_works: Repetition + dialogue novelty.
how_to_shoot: Record 3 takes, play on devices, film the desk.
detection_cues: 0s several screens with same face; 0.5s one speaks; 1s another responds; 1.5s continues.

name: Vanish / Magic Disappear
what_you_see: Object or person disappears with a snap/poof effect.
why_it_works: Object permanence violation.
how_to_shoot: Make the clutter vanish, leaving organizer.
detection_cues: 0s object present; 0.5s gesture; 1s object gone; 1.5s clean scene.

name: Giant / Miniature Scale Illusion
what_you_see: Product appears huge next to people/buildings or creator appears tiny.
why_it_works: Scale violation grabs attention instantly.
how_to_shoot: Forced perspective: product close to lens, person far away 'holding' it.
detection_cues: 0s scale mismatch; 0.5s interaction; 1s mismatch persists; 1.5s reveal of trick or not.

name: FOOH / CGI Product Stunt
what_you_see: CGI product doing the impossible in real environment (giant lipstick on a bus, bottle on a building).
why_it_works: Looks real yet impossible.
how_to_shoot: AI video generator composite of product over city skyline.
detection_cues: 0s real location with oversized CGI product; 0.5s product moving; 1s people react; 1.5s.

name: AI Morph / Transformation
what_you_see: One object/person morphs smoothly into another (old product morphs into new).
why_it_works: Continuous impossible change.
how_to_shoot: Morph competitor bottle into your bottle.
detection_cues: 0s object A; 0.5s blending; 1s object B; 1.5s hold.

name: Mask Reveal Transition
what_you_see: A new scene appears within a moving object's silhouette (door, arm, product).
why_it_works: Layered reveal.
how_to_shoot: Mask 'after' scene within the product as it passes.
detection_cues: 0s scene A; 0.5s object shows scene B within it; 1s scene B full; 1.5s hold.

name: Zoom Out Reveal
what_you_see: Starts extreme close on a detail, pulls out to reveal full surprising context.
why_it_works: Recontextualization payoff.
how_to_shoot: Close on texture; pull back to show it's the product in use.
detection_cues: 0s abstract close texture; 0.5s widening; 1s context emerging; 1.5s full reveal.

name: X-Ray / Cutaway 3D
what_you_see: 3D render showing inside body/product (how it works).
why_it_works: Seeing the invisible.
how_to_shoot: 3D animation of product fibers or gut bacteria.
detection_cues: 0s rendered 3D internal view; 0.5s animated; 1s callout; 1.5s continues.

name: Sunglasses Text Reflection
what_you_see: Zoom into sunglasses lenses reflecting a screen with the key message.
why_it_works: Hidden message in reflection = discovery.
how_to_shoot: Creator in shades facing laptop with claim; zoom into reflection.
detection_cues: 0s face with sunglasses; 0.5s zooming; 1s reflection text readable; 1.5s hold.

name: High Motion Base B-Roll
what_you_see: The base footage itself contains high motion (sports, vehicles, crowds, splashes).
why_it_works: Motion-rich frames beat static talking heads.
how_to_shoot: Use product in motion: bike ride, workout, pouring.
detection_cues: 0s lots of motion across frame; 0.5s continues; 1s continues; 1.5s continues.

name: Unusual First Image/Scene
what_you_see: A full-screen image or scene that visually breaks convention (odd object, bizarre place).
why_it_works: Novelty detection.
how_to_shoot: Product in a bizarre spot (bathtub full of product).
detection_cues: 0s unusual composition; 0.5s held; 1s maybe creator; 1.5s continues.

name: Silent Reaction PIP
what_you_see: Base clip plays while creator in a small corner box watches silently, then reacts.
why_it_works: Emotional contagion; curiosity about reaction.
how_to_shoot: Founder in corner watching a customer video, reacts.
detection_cues: 0s base clip + small face box; 0.5s silent face; 1s reaction; 1.5s talk.

name: Visual Mistake
what_you_see: Something that looks like an error (misplaced object, weird crop, mis-framed shot).
why_it_works: Brain fixates on anomalies.
how_to_shoot: Leave a deliberate 'mistake' (camera upside down, product half-out).
detection_cues: 0s anomalous element; 0.5s still there; 1s continues; 1.5s.

name: Macro ASMR Close-Up
what_you_see: Extreme macro of texture: cream swirl, fabric weave, bubbles.
why_it_works: Sensory detail rarely seen; ASMR satisfaction.
how_to_shoot: Macro lens on product texture.
detection_cues: 0s abstract texture filling frame; 0.5s movement; 1s detail; 1.5s pull back.

name: Oddly Satisfying Process
what_you_see: Perfectly clean process: peeling film, cutting, pressure washing, perfect fit.
why_it_works: Completion satisfaction.
how_to_shoot: Peel protective film off product; pressure wash a stain.
detection_cues: 0s process start; 0.5s partially done; 1s progress; 1.5s near-complete.

name: Gross / Problem Close-Up
what_you_see: Close-up of the problem: dirty filter, blackheads, stain, mold.
why_it_works: Disgust grabs attention; self-check.
how_to_shoot: Show the gunk in an old pillow.
detection_cues: 0s repellent problem visual; 0.5s closer; 1s more; 1.5s product appears.

name: Before/After Result Shot
what_you_see: Opens directly on the result or side-by-side before/after.
why_it_works: Instant proof payoff.
how_to_shoot: Show result first, then how.
detection_cues: 0s after state or split; 0.5s same; 1s before shown; 1.5s.

name: Unusual Location
what_you_see: Creator in odd place: shopping cart, washing machine, car trunk, freezer aisle.
why_it_works: Setting incongruity.
how_to_shoot: Pitch skincare sitting in a bathtub full of clothes.
detection_cues: 0s atypical location; 0.5s creator speaking; 1s location obvious; 1.5s continues.

name: Absurd Prop
what_you_see: Creator uses an absurd prop (banana as microphone, giant clock).
why_it_works: Humor + incongruity.
how_to_shoot: Oversized prop version of product.
detection_cues: 0s prop visible; 0.5s use; 1s creator; 1.5s continues.

name: Out-of-Place Element
what_you_see: Orderly scene with one element clearly not belonging.
why_it_works: Anomaly detection.
how_to_shoot: Neat vanity with a live lobster beside product.
detection_cues: 0s orderly frame + anomaly; 0.5s anomaly moves; 1s; 1.5s.

name: First-Person POV Hands
what_you_see: Camera at eye level showing the viewer's own hands using the product.
why_it_works: Self-projection.
how_to_shoot: Chest mount or head-height shot of hands opening the product.
detection_cues: 0s hands in foreground from bottom edge; 0.5s interacting; 1s; 1.5s.

name: CCTV / Security Cam Look
what_you_see: Grainy, high-angle, timestamped security footage.
why_it_works: Voyeuristic realism.
how_to_shoot: Doorbell-cam style: package delivered, dog steals.
detection_cues: 0s fisheye high angle + timestamp; 0.5s action; 1s; 1.5s.

name: Celebrity / Famous Clip
what_you_see: Recognizable celebrity/meme face in the first frame.
why_it_works: Face recognition triggers attention.
how_to_shoot: Licensed or meme clip relevant to benefit (use carefully).
detection_cues: 0s famous face; 0.5s; 1s; 1.5s cut.

name: Animal / Pet Hook
what_you_see: Pet in frame doing something cute or funny with product.
why_it_works: Universally attractive stimulus.
how_to_shoot: Dog 'reviewing' the pet product.
detection_cues: 0s animal visible; 0.5s action; 1s; 1.5s product.

name: Baby / Kid Hook
what_you_see: Baby or child in frame reacting/using product.
why_it_works: Protective attention bias.
how_to_shoot: Toddler trying the product with parent reaction.
detection_cues: 0s child; 0.5s action; 1s reaction; 1.5s.

name: Creative Absurd Demo
what_you_see: Product demonstrated on an unexpected object (tomato, egg, balloon).
why_it_works: Absurdity is memorable.
how_to_shoot: Apply concealer to a tomato with eyes cut out.
detection_cues: 0s odd object; 0.5s product applied; 1s effect visible; 1.5s.

name: Lab / Side-by-Side Experiment
what_you_see: Two containers/samples side by side with labels being tested.
why_it_works: Evidence framing.
how_to_shoot: Two cups: competitor vs yours.
detection_cues: 0s two labeled samples; 0.5s test begins; 1s divergence; 1.5s.

name: Microscope View
what_you_see: Microscope/magnified imagery of skin, fabric, bacteria.
why_it_works: Invisible world revealed.
how_to_shoot: USB microscope on skin before/after.
detection_cues: 0s magnified circle; 0.5s; 1s; 1.5s.

name: Chaos / Mess Scene
what_you_see: Opens on a messy, chaotic room/situation.
why_it_works: Disorder draws scanning.
how_to_shoot: Messy closet before organizer.
detection_cues: 0s cluttered frame; 0.5s; 1s creator; 1.5s.

name: Window Watching Scenario
what_you_see: Creator peeks out window at someone with product.
why_it_works: Voyeurism + intrigue.
how_to_shoot: Peek through blinds at neighbor with product.
detection_cues: 0s blinds/window; 0.5s creator peering; 1s POV of outside; 1.5s.

name: Megaphone Announcement
what_you_see: Creator shouting through a megaphone.
why_it_works: Urgency and noise cue.
how_to_shoot: Announce sale through megaphone.
detection_cues: 0s megaphone; 0.5s; 1s; 1.5s.

name: Car Talking Head
what_you_see: Creator in driver's seat talking, parked.
why_it_works: Native, authentic UGC setting.
how_to_shoot: Film car review for car accessory.
detection_cues: 0s car interior; 0.5s talking; 1s; 1.5s.

name: Lo-Fi Native Selfie
what_you_see: Vertical front-camera selfie, casual lighting, no graphics.
why_it_works: Looks like a friend's post.
how_to_shoot: Creator's phone front cam in real home.
detection_cues: 0s arm-length selfie; 0.5s talking; 1s; 1.5s.

name: Low-Angle Hero Product
what_you_see: Low-angle product shot with dramatic lighting.
why_it_works: Monumentality.
how_to_shoot: Shoot product from table level against backlight.
detection_cues: 0s product large from below; 0.5s light; 1s rotation; 1.5s.

name: Archival / Vintage Footage
what_you_see: Old film grain footage or historical photo.
why_it_works: Nostalgia + contrast.
how_to_shoot: Vintage ad clip then modern product.
detection_cues: 0s grainy footage; 0.5s; 1s; 1.5s cut.

name: Empty Shelves / Sold Out
what_you_see: Empty store shelves or 'sold out' signs.
why_it_works: Scarcity.
how_to_shoot: Film empty display in store.
detection_cues: 0s empty shelves; 0.5s pan; 1s sign; 1.5s.

name: Cloud Message Mystery
what_you_see: Creator points skyward, then holds up sign.
why_it_works: Curiosity build.
how_to_shoot: Point up; sign with value prop.
detection_cues: 0s pointing up; 0.5s; 1s sign; 1.5s.

name: 3D Talking Character
what_you_see: Frame 1 is a 3D/Pixar-style or claymation character (an organ, pill, body part, germ, animal or product) looking at camera and talking, often in a real-world set.
why_it_works: An unexpected cartoon character in a feed of real people breaks the pattern and personifies the problem.
how_to_shoot: Generate a character of the problem (e.g. a tired liver, a hair follicle) with an AI image/video tool and have it deliver line 1 straight to camera.
detection_cues: Non-human 3D/clay character with a face in the first frame, mouth moving across 0-1.5s.

name: Tier List Board
what_you_see: Opens on an S/A/B/C/F tier-list board being filled with products or options.
why_it_works: Rankings trigger opinion and the urge to see where their pick lands.
how_to_shoot: Screen-record or overlay a tier board; drag competitors into low tiers and your product into S tier.
detection_cues: Coloured tier rows labelled S/A/B/C in the first second.

name: Yap Cold Open
what_you_see: Frame 1 is the creator already mid-sentence and mid-gesture (often walking or leaning toward the lens). No intro, no settling in: the video feels like you dropped into a conversation already in motion.
why_it_works: Skipping the wind-up removes the dead first half-second where viewers swipe. Energy plus movement from frame 1 reads as 'something is already happening'.
how_to_shoot: Start recording, talk for 2-3 seconds, then cut the clip so it opens mid-word while you're moving toward camera holding the product. Title text on screen carries the hook.
detection_cues: 0s creator already mid-word with mouth open/gesturing; 0.5-3s continuous talking, often moving toward lens; no intro pause or settling.
source: Kallaway Short-Form Lego Bricks FigJam (Visual Hooks #20). Definition inferred: card text not readable without Figma login
